title: Events
sub: A delegate outsiders can only subscribe to
cards/0/body:
A public delegate field is dangerous: anyone can invoke it or wipe out every subscriber with =.

event leaves outsiders only += and -=. Only the owning class can raise the event.
cards/1/q: Which line will not compile outside the Button class?
cards/1/explain: From the outside an event only has += and -=. You cannot assign or invoke it.
cards/2/options/0: With no subscribers the event is null — without ?. you get a NullReferenceException
cards/2/explain: An event with no subscribers is null.
cards/3/body: By convention a handler receives the sender and the arguments: EventHandler<TArgs>.
cards/4/title: A subscription holds on to the subscriber
cards/4/body: The publisher stores the delegate, and the delegate stores a reference to the subscriber object. As long as the publisher is alive and you have not unsubscribed, the garbage collector will not collect the subscriber. The classic leak: a window subscribes to a global event and never unsubscribes.
cards/5/q: A window subscribed to the static event App.ThemeChanged and closed without unsubscribing. What happens?
cards/5/options/0: The window stays in memory: the event holds a reference to it
cards/5/options/1: The garbage collector collects the window
cards/5/options/2: The event unsubscribes the closed window by itself
cards/5/explain: More on this in ".NET under the hood", in the "Garbage collection and resources" unit.
cards/6/q: Raise the event only if there are subscribers
cards/7/pairs/2/1: Raise only if there are subscribers
cards/7/pairs/3/1: Unsubscribe and let the object go
cards/8/options/0: Only the owning class can raise an event
cards/8/options/1: An event with no subscribers is null
cards/8/options/2: A subscription keeps the subscriber in memory
cards/8/options/3: Outsiders can clear an event with =
cards/8/explain: Blocking = from the outside is exactly what event is for.
